\section[tiṇḍi]{\kn{ತಿಂಡಿ} (tiṇḍi) — a snack, a light meal}

\label{lesson:KA-C94-snack}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for a wound, then the Kannada for vomiting.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ತಿಂಡಿ}}
\textbf{\kn{ತಿಂಡಿ}} (\emph{tiṇḍi}) — \textquotedblleft{}a snack, a light meal\textquotedblright{}, also the word for breakfast. It comes from \textbf{\kn{ತಿನ್ನು}} (\emph{tinnu}), \textquotedblleft{}to eat\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\kn{ತಿಂಡಿ} \kn{ಆಯ್ತಾ}?} (\emph{tiṇḍi āytā?}) — \textquotedblleft{}have you had breakfast?\textquotedblright{}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Something to eat, from the verb to eat.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tiṇḍi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tiṇḍi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{tiṇḍi āytā?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for a wound, then the Kannada for vomiting, then say \emph{tiṇḍi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ತಿಂಡಿ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A snack, a light meal\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[camaca]{\kn{ಚಮಚ} (camaca) — a spoon}

\label{lesson:KA-C94-spoon}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for vomiting, then the Kannada for a snack.

\textbf{\kn{ಒಂದು} \kn{ಚಮಚ} \kn{ಕೊಡಿ}} (\emph{ondu camaca koḍi}) — \textquotedblleft{}please give me a spoon\textquotedblright{}.

A first thing to ask for at the table.
\end{grammarlens}
